headline: 30 killed by floods and landslides in 5 Chattogram division districts
summary: Cox's Bazar was the hardest hit with 19 deaths, as the government opens over 1,000 shelters for thousands of displaced people.
details: Disaster Management and Relief Minister Asadul Habib Dulu confirmed that 30 people have died due to recent floods and landslides triggered by heavy rainfall in five districts of the Chattogram division.
The casualties are distributed across the region: 19 people died in Cox's Bazar, five each in Chattogram and Bandarban, and one in Rangamati.
To support the displaced, the government has opened 1,057 shelters across the affected districts, with 640 in Cox's Bazar and 220 in Bandarban.
Over 12,000 people have taken refuge in these shelters, including 8,340 in Chattogram and 2,173 in Bandarban.
The government has allocated significant financial aid and rice supplies to the affected districts, including additional funds approved on Thursday to strengthen the response.
The Prime Minister's Relief and Welfare Fund has also provided Tk 20 lakh for each of the five affected districts.
Minister Dulu highlighted the recurring danger of landslides and announced plans to rehabilitate families living on vulnerable hill slopes by building houses on government land.
State Minister for Land and Chattogram Hill Tracts Affairs Mir Mohammed Helal Uddin added that 1,300 metric tonnes of rice were distributed across the three hill districts yesterday.

headline: 190 hospitalized as two more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services reports that total deaths this year have risen to 24, with 7,747 cases recorded.
details: At least two dengue patients died and 190 others were hospitalized within a 24-hour period ending at 8:00 am today.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), one death was reported in the Khulna division and another in Dhaka North City Corporation.
With these latest figures, the total number of dengue deaths this year has risen to 24, while total cases have reached 7,747.
Currently, 655 dengue patients are receiving treatment at various hospitals across the country.
